name: Potato salad
summary: Tender potatoes and chopped boiled egg folded through a tangy mayonnaise dressing with spring onion and parsley: the salad no braai is complete without.
about: Potato salad, aartappelslaai in Afrikaans, is the salad most South African families bring to a braai, a Christmas table or a church lunch. Recipes differ from home to home: some sweeten the dressing, others add mustard, gherkins or crispy bacon, but egg and mayonnaise are almost always in.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: waxy, peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes

steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water and add the salt. Bring to the boil over high heat, then simmer for 10–12 minutes, until a knife slides in easily but the cubes still hold their shape.
At the same time, lower the eggs into a small pot of boiling water and boil for 10 minutes. Move them to a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes, then peel and chop.
Drain the potatoes well, tip them into a large bowl and sprinkle over 1 tbsp of the vinegar while hot, so they soak it up. Leave to cool for about 30 minutes, until just warm.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, sugar and the remaining vinegar together until smooth.
Add the dressing, chopped eggs, spring onions and most of the parsley to the potatoes and fold gently until everything is coated. Season with salt and pepper.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so the flavours settle, then scatter with the rest of the parsley and serve cold.
prepNote: Make up to a day ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Don't leave it in the sun for more than an hour.
